    AI Overview
    View all
    Loose bodies in the elbow are small fragments of bone or cartilage that break off and float within the joint, often causing pain, locking, swelling, and stiffness. Primarily caused by injury (trauma) or osteoarthritis, these fragments can hinder movement. Treatment ranges from physical therapy to arthroscopic surgery. 
    Symptoms
     
    • Catching or locking: The elbow may lock in place or produce a clicking sound.
    • Pain and swelling: Discomfort is common, particularly with movement.
    • Reduced range of motion: Difficulty fully straightening or bending the arm. 
    Causes 
    • Trauma: Fractures or dislocations.
    • Osteoarthritis: Wear and tear creating loose bone spurs.
    • Osteochondritis dissecans: Separation of cartilage from the bone.
    • Other: Rheumatoid or septic arthritis. 
    Diagnosis 
    • Physical Exam: A specialist evaluates movement and pain.
    • Imaging: X-rays are common, though MRI scans or CT scans are often used to identify the precise location and size of the loose bodies. 
    Treatment Options 
    • Non-Surgical: For mild symptoms, rest, medication, and physical therapy can help.
    • Elbow Arthroscopy: A minimally invasive surgery is commonly used to remove the fragments.
    • Open Surgery: Sometimes necessary to remove larger fragments. 
    Recovery from arthroscopic removal typically takes 6-8 weeks for a full return to activity.
